title: 2013 HMMT February Guts Problem 7
statement: Find the number of positive divisors \(d\) of \(15!=15 \cdot 14 \cdots 2 \cdot 1\) such that \(\operatorname{gcd}(d, 60)=5\).

solutions.text: 36 Since \(\operatorname{gcd}(d, 60)=5\), we know that \(d=5^{i} d^{\prime}\) for some integer \(i>0\) and some integer \(d^{\prime}\) which is relatively prime to 60 . Consequently, \(d^{\prime}\) is a divisor of \((15!) / 5\); eliminating common factors with 60 gives that \(d^{\prime}\) is a factor of \(\left(7^{2}\right)(11)(13)\), which has \((2+1)(1+1)(1+1)=12\) factors. Finally, \(i\) can be 1,2 , or 3 , so there are a total of \(3 \cdot 12=36\) possibilities.
